about: Before/after proof (evals/kb-proof.ts). Robin's fixture, eight months on: 45 pages, a rule that changed on the same page, a newer rule on a page the question doesn't point to, a stale page with a newer one beside it, and 15 distractor pages. Every case is something a model can't guess without Robin's notes. `include`: regexes the reply must match (case-insensitive). `exclude`: must not match. `judge`: a rubric a second T3 run scores 0-2. A case passes when every regex holds and the judge, if any, gives 2. Version 2 (round 7): the `friday` case no longer depends on today's real weekday (v1 asked as if it were Friday, and workers corrected it from the clock); four more changed rules were added to the fixture, which also changed the right answers of `flags` and `payload-retention`. No case was changed to fit a result. v1 results stay in ~/serra-notes/kb-growth/evals/proof-r6-claude/.

cases.text: what are my two priorities this quarter?
if I ping Robin on a Friday afternoon, will they answer quickly?
cases.judge: Robin's Fridays are focus days (no meetings, slow replies). 2 = says replies will be slow because Friday is a focus day; 1 = vague; 0 = says Robin will answer quickly, or invents other hours.

cases.text: who needs to sign off before we deploy the refunds release?
who gets to decide whether we support JPY refunds, product or eng?
cases.judge: Priya (product) decides scope; Robin decides how. 2 = says Priya decides whether; 1 = names Priya without the split; 0 = says eng or Robin decides.

cases.text: I've never cut a Ledgerline release. what are the steps?
payments look down for everyone right now, what do I do first?
how much discount can I offer Brightmoor again?
what format do our invoice numbers use?
how long do we keep webhook payloads?
cases.judge: An older page (confirmed 2026-04-01) says webhook payloads are kept 30 days; a newer page (confirmed 2026-11-12) says 14 days. 2 = says 14 days is current; 1 = both without picking, or asks; 0 = says 30 days.

cases.text: when does the sandbox get wiped?
how fast should I roll out a new feature flag?
cases.judge: An older page (confirmed 2026-05-01) says flags roll out 5%, 25%, 100% over three days; a newer page (confirmed 2026-11-05) says 10%, 50%, 100% over two days. 2 = gives 10/50/100 as current; 1 = both without picking, or asks; 0 = gives 5/25/100.

cases.text: can merchants get refunds in yen?
cases.judge: JPY is not planned (no minor-unit handling); live currencies are EUR and GBP, USD next. 2 = says no and why or which are live; 1 = says no only; 0 = says yes.

cases.text: which day do risky releases ship these days?
cases.judge: The working-style page says risky releases used to ship on Tuesday and, since 2026-10-01, ship on Thursday. 2 = says Thursday is current (may mention the old Tuesday rule); 1 = gives both without picking or asks; 0 = says Tuesday.

cases.text: a merchant is getting 429s, what is our API rate limit per merchant?
cases.judge: An older page (confirmed 2026-06-01) says 100 requests per second; a newer page on plans (confirmed 2026-10-20) says 250. 2 = says 250 is the current limit; 1 = gives both without picking, or asks; 0 = says 100.

cases.text: when is the on-call handover now?
cases.judge: The rota page (confirmed 2026-05-01) says Monday 10:00; a newer note (confirmed 2026-11-10) says the handover moved to Tuesday at 09:00. 2 = Tuesday 09:00 as current; 1 = both without picking, or asks; 0 = Monday 10:00.

cases.text: can we ship the risky webhook change this Friday?
cases.judge: Risky releases never ship on Friday (Thursday is the day). 2 = says no and points to Thursday; 1 = says no without a day; 0 = says yes.

cases.text: what's the max PR size these days?
cases.judge: The working-style page says PRs under 400 changed lines, and a newer line on the same page (since 2026-09-15) says under 300. 2 = says 300 is current; 1 = both without picking, or asks; 0 = says 400.

cases.text: what time do FX rates update each day?
cases.judge: An older page says FX rates come from the treasury feed at 06:00 UTC; a newer page (confirmed 2026-10-30) says 05:00 UTC. 2 = 05:00 UTC as current; 1 = both without picking, or asks; 0 = 06:00.
